evals.name: distinctive-public-program-deck
evals.prompt: Create a six-slide reveal.js presentation for a public library's digital literacy program. The audience is older adults and the room is bright. Use a calm, approachable visual direction, speaker notes, and meaningful visual evidence. Deliver HTML and CSS files.
evals.expected_output: A distinctive light presentation whose narrative, imagery, typography, and varied compositions suit older adults and a bright room without borrowing Cisco styling.
assertions: The slide sequence has a clear audience promise, supporting evidence, and concrete final action
At least three content-specific compositions are used rather than repeating one card grid
Visual evidence is prominent and any missing asset is represented by an honest, clearly labeled placeholder
Typography, contrast, density, and notes are appropriate for older adults in a bright room
The deck uses valid Reveal markup and pinned dependencies without loading unrelated libraries
Rendered desktop and mobile screenshots show no overflow, overlap, or unreadably small text

evals.name: product-evidence-walkthrough
evals.prompt: Build a seven-slide reveal.js walkthrough for a passwordless sign-in product. Show the current pain, the sign-in flow, real product screens, a before-and-after comparison, and a three-step adoption path. Use modern icons and restrained animation.
evals.expected_output: A product-led deck with screenshots as evidence, a readable system flow, parallel before-and-after states, and a concrete action path rather than a generic feature-card presentation.
assertions: The product and literal audience benefit appear in the first viewport
Screenshots or clearly labeled screenshot placeholders receive more visual weight than explanatory copy
The sign-in flow communicates causal order with stable nodes and subordinate connectors
Before and after states are structurally parallel and do not rely on color alone
Fragments follow the spoken sequence and reduced-motion behavior preserves all meaning
Lucide icons support visible labels and do not replace substantive visual evidence

evals.name: preserve-existing-design-language
evals.prompt: Add two slides to an existing branded reveal.js presentation: one system diagram and one final call to action. Match the existing presentation closely, improve any obvious accessibility problems you touch, and do not redesign the rest of the deck.
evals.expected_output: Two new slides that look native to the supplied deck, reuse its tokens and motifs, introduce only necessary styles, and leave unrelated markup unchanged.
assertions: The new slides reuse the existing palette, typography, frame, spacing, and recurring motifs
The system diagram and call to action use different compositions suited to their content
No generic starter theme or unrelated visual language is imposed
Changes remain scoped to the requested slides and shared styles they require
Touched icons, focus states, contrast, and meaningful imagery remain accessible
Browser validation confirms the additions do not overflow or break existing navigation

evals.name: underspecified-animation-request
evals.prompt: Add animations to my reveal.js presentation so it feels more polished.
evals.expected_output: One concise clarification question that recommends a likely motion approach based on narrative purpose without editing files prematurely.
assertions: The response asks one concise question about what the motion should communicate
It recommends a likely Reveal mechanism instead of dumping an exhaustive feature list
It distinguishes sequence, pacing, continuity, code focus, and custom motion only as needed
It does not animate every element or add a community plugin by default
